transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jared Mills (Nimbus VP Eng), Sonia Patel (Nimbus Head of AI), Marcus Lee (Nimbus SRE)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick agenda  recap last week's perf numbers, talk canary/ab rollout plan, monitoring and runbooks, and confirm next steps. Is that OK?
[00:12] Jared Mills: Yep that's perfect. We did a quick readout with the execs yesterday, they want a clear cutover plan, timeline, and fallbacks.
[00:20] Sonia Patel: also want to make sure latency doesn't spike for the payments flow, that's the critical path.
[00:30] Priya Desai: Great. Quick perf recap  since last week, the POC on Redwood Dedicated with the quantized model saw p95 token latency at ~135ms for 1k token sessions in staging, and throughput looked linear up to our reserved GPU pool. We did see a KV cache miss pattern causing some bursts during warmup.
[01:05] Marcus Lee: That KV cache note  can you say more about the miss pattern? Is it due to sharding or TTL?
[01:12] Priya Desai: Mostly prefix diversity; some sessions have unique prefixes so cache hit rate drops. We recommended small prefix normalization in the client and pre-warming the cache for the payment flows. Also suggesting short-lived pinning for hot sessions during the canary window.
[01:35] Jared Mills: Sounds reasonable. For cutover planning, we have two windows: weekend low-traffic (Saturday 02:00-06:00 UTC) and a weekday night (Tuesday 22:00-02:00). Ops prefers the weekend but execs want shorter exposure and faster rollback options.
[02:05] Alex Chen: Typical tradeoff. We usually recommend a staged canary starting with 1% production traffic -> 5% -> 25% over 24-48 hours, with objective gates in between. For a payments-critical path you might prefer a tighter ramp and more monitoring hooks. We can also do an A/B style run where a small percentage routes to Redwood and responses are compared for correctness and latency.
[02:45] Sonia Patel: On correctness, we have strict acceptance criteria: parity on core decisioning for auth flows (match rate >= 99.5%), no increased latency above +50ms p95, and no increased error/invoice failures. We also need audit logs and evidence for SOC2 reviewers.
[03:10] Priya Desai: We have the audit logging pipeline for Private and Dedicated  request/response logs can be pushed to your S3 or KMS-encrypted bucket. We support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS. For SOC2 evidence we'll share the runbook and monitoring snapshots.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: Great. On monitoring: what dashboards do you recommend? We want end-to-end: request latency, token-level latency, cache hit rate, model quality regression (sampled deltas), and error budgets. Also alert thresholds.
[04:00] Alex Chen: We'll share a monitoring dashboard template  prometheus + grafana friendly, plus a lightweight SLO table. Alerting: p95 latency > baseline + 40ms, error rate > 0.5% for auth flows, and model mismatch > threshold on sampled evals. We'll include runbook steps for each alert.
[04:35] Jared Mills: For rollback, what's the fastest path? Re-route traffic back to current provider, or switch model variant?
[04:45] Priya Desai: Fastest is routing policy rollback: we can fail traffic back to existing endpoints within seconds using smart routing policies. Model variant fallback is also supported but more disruptive. We'll include both in the runbook with explicit steps and verification checks.
[05:10] Sonia Patel: Are there any compliance blockers for canary? Our legal team wants data residency logs and proof we don't retain PII. Also SSO integration must be configured for access to the console.
[05:25] Alex Chen: We can scope the canary to obfuscated payloads, and logs can be redacted; retention configs are editable. SAML SSO and RBAC are standard for Dedicated and Private; we'll include the SSO enablement checklist in the handover docs.
[05:50] Marcus Lee: On the practical side, we want to run a shadow test first where all traffic is duplicated to Redwood but not served. That gives us a correctness baseline without risk.
[06:02] Alex Chen: Totally. Shadowing + a 1% canary is the lower-risk path. For the shadow test we'll need a two-hour snapshot with full payloads, plus sampling for quality checks. We'll prepare a side-by-side comparison script.
[06:28] Jared Mills: What about DB migrations or schema changes? Our payment flow touches fraud scoring which depends on some feature flags.
[06:36] Priya Desai: No infra migration needed on your DB for the model cutover. Just ensure feature-flag parity in the canary environment; we recommend toggling non-critical flags off to reduce variability. We'll add a checklist item.
[06:55] Alex Chen: Let's map the runbook high level: pre-canary checks (feature flags, pre-warm cache, access controls, SSO, retention), shadow run (2 hours), 1% canary with metric gates, ramp to 5%/25% as long as gates pass, full cutover with rollback plan. Each step has explicit verification.
[07:20] Sonia Patel: For the metric gates, can we get automated gating? Like a Prometheus alert that fails the gate and triggers rollback automation?
[07:30] Priya Desai: We can integrate gates with your orchestration. We offer webhook hooks for gating  if a gate trips, we can automatically scale down canary or flip routing. We'll document the automation and provide example scripts.
[07:50] Marcus Lee: Any recommended length for each ramp? Given our risk tolerance, maybe 6-12 hours between ramps?
[07:58] Alex Chen: That's a reasonable conservative approach. For payments I'd recommend at least 6 hours per step with continuous monitoring and a hold period after each ramp to validate spikes.
[08:16] Jared Mills: Who owns the roll? Redwood or Nimbus ops during the canary and cutover?
[08:22] Alex Chen: We usually operate a co-managed plan: Redwood runs the canary orchestration and provides runbook/automation; Nimbus executes final cutover approval and has the single-click ability to failback. We'll include an approvals matrix in the runbook.
[08:42] Sonia Patel: Ok. For post-go-live support  do you offer an elevated on-call for the first 72 hours?
[08:50] Alex Chen: Yes, we offer a proactive 72-hour monitoring support option as an add-on; we'll include that in the proposal and costs. It includes daily rollups and a dedicated engineer on-call for critical escalations.
[09:05] Jared Mills: Cost: need an estimate of incremental cost during the canary and ramp. Also what's the expected per-token unit change with quantization and KV caching?
[09:18] Priya Desai: Quantization reduced token cost ~20% in our POC numbers; KV caching further reduces cost on repeated prefixes. We'll send a modeled cost spreadsheet based on your traffic profile. During canary we recommend reserving some Dedicated capacity to avoid throttling.
[09:40] Alex Chen: Action items recap and dates  we want to make sure there are clear owners.
[09:48] Priya Desai: Action items  Redwood to produce canary playbook + template, monitoring dashboard, and automation examples by Friday 2025-08-08. Nimbus to confirm cutover windows and acceptance criteria by Sunday 2025-08-10. Schedule shadow test and 1% canary run (tentative week of 2025-08-15).
[10:20] Jared Mills: Sounds good. Any outstanding risks we should flag?
[10:25] Marcus Lee: Cache cold-starts and unique prefixes are a real risk; also model delta causing rare regressions in auth heuristics.
[10:33] Priya Desai: We'll include a sampling plan to catch regressions and a fast rollback plan. Also suggest a small synthetic traffic generator to exercise edge cases during the shadow run.
[10:50] Alex Chen: Great. Last thing  I'll email the runbook link and canary playbook and set up a 90-minute canary dry-run the week before cutover. Thanks everyone.
[11:05] Jared Mills: Thanks all.

Auto-summary (optional):
- Agreed co-managed canary approach: shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> cutover
- Must meet acceptance criteria: 99.5% decision parity, p95 +50ms cap, error budget intact
- Redwood to deliver playbooks, dashboards, automation by 2025-08-08
- Nimbus to confirm cutover window and final acceptance criteria by 2025-08-10

References/attachments: canary-playbook-v1 (link to deck), monitoring-dashboard.json (Grafana export), cost-model.xlsx (link)

End of transcript.
